ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so route deviation is measured in kilometres and feeds the fare, not a fixed quote [F1][F7]. One off-route segment is recorded: 17:24–17:40, 10.28 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, adding 7.53 km and reaching up to 2273 m from the optimal route, i.e. an unexplained deviation by a driver [F3][RD-1]. No traffic incident exists on the replaced stretch, and a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment [F12][F15][RD-4]. The driver's statement is not consent because a "rider said it was fine" claim appearing only in the statement, written after the trip, is a claim and not a rider message [F11][RD-5].

The rider did agree before the segment started: at 17:20 the driver asked whether to take another way because of the jam building up on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, and at 17:21 — before the 17:24 segment start — the rider replied "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间", i.e. a general authorisation to take whichever way is faster to get to VivoCity [F8][F9][RD-5]. Under RD-5 such a general route choice covers a route chosen to reach the destination, but not an errand or loop of the driver's own; here that general authorisation is given, and the excess distance billed to the rider is $11.56 (8.20 km × $1.4099/km, this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km) [F4][F7][F9][RD-5].

The question the trace leaves open is whether the record ties the driven 10.28 km segment to any agreed route. There is no rider-named stop anywhere in the record — the chat records no place the rider asked to stop at, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt anything [F8][F9][RD-3]. Nothing in the chat, statement or fact table puts the car on a particular named road during 17:24–17:40, and the driver's own statement says only that he "went round" without naming a route [F8][F9][F11]. The record therefore does not settle whether the authorised faster route is the one actually driven: the agreement to any faster way is general, and the only general-route reading available is whether the loop actually served the destination, which the record cannot confirm. On this record the finding is undetermined [RD-5]. Because this segment is the only off-route segment and it changes both the amount and any account action, the case goes to a person: ruling escalate, amount null.
